abstract: Readers of a long series need a character reference that stops where their reading does. Filtering retrieval by position is not enough: a whole-series index, the generator’s memory and shared page surfaces can each carry later information onto an early page. NARRATIVEWIKI turns a novel series into a linked character wiki per reading cutoff: each fact carries its first supporting volume and a verbatim quote, and a page for cutoff t is assembled from facts of volumes ≤t before generation. In a pilot on five public-domain books (111 gold facts; LLM-annotated labels, a sample humanreviewed), when only the reader’s volumes reached the generator, systems stated no later fact and implied one (1 of 880 reads), against 4 of 220 from memory and 8 of 220 from the full text under instruction; our search misses three in ten seeded implied disclosures. NARRATIVEWIKI conveys fewer gold facts than longcontext prompting (0.802 against 0.848) and its citations establish fewer assertions (0.512 against 0.658). On a renamed, paraphrased text, closed-book recall falls from 0.683 to 0.003 while reading systems lose at most 0.070, and NARRATIVEWIKI states a later marriage (4 of 220) from a character’s prediction. We release gold facts, labels and tools.
